semantics: docs/specs/timers.md §4 (the fold), §2.3 (timing), as changed by docs/specs/timers2.md §3 (fold v4; its §3.4 pseudocode is normative). Parse every `at` to integer epoch milliseconds, truncating sub-millisecond digits (never rounding, never through a float or a Date); all arithmetic is integer.

fold(run_id, timer, events, frozen): `timer` is timer_sets[case.timer], a normalised Timer v2 (timers2.md §1); the fold reads its steps and lap types only. Events are in server arrival order. Pass 1, arrival: skip an id already seen (ids compared lowercase; the first occurrence wins); `finish` gets no effect (the server decides it); with `frozen`, every event at arrival index >= frozen.after is void with frozen.reason and not folded; a `start` is applied if its id is run_id, else void `merged`; the first `stop`/`discard` is the terminal, later ones void `already_closed`; a `stop` before the start is void `before_start`, one more than max_run_ms after it void `too_long`, whenever it arrives (checked before `already_closed`), and neither closes the run. A stop ends the open reopen transaction.

Pass 1, reopen (target = a stop): `no_target` unless that stop was seen; `already_closed` when the terminal is a discard; `not_stopped` unless the target is the current terminal; `stale` if at <= the stop's at; `too_long` past max_run_ms; else applied: the terminal clears, (stop, reopen) is the open transaction and a role pair. A discard while a transaction is open reverts it: the reopen becomes void `reverted`, the stop is the terminal again (re-applied if it had been removed, that remove void `no_target`), the pair is no longer a role, and the discard is applied. remove: `no_target` unless the target was seen, isn't removed yet, at > target.at, and it is a pause, a lap, or a stop of a current role pair (that stop becomes void `deleted`; its reopen stays applied). No 7-day bound on remove. Effects are recomputed from scratch on every fold.

Pass 2, by (at, rank, lowercase id) ascending: each role pair's stop is a gap pause (rank 0, id = the stop's; left out when the stop is removed) and its reopen a gap resume (rank 2, id = the reopen's); user events rank 1, where a resume with the same at as the pause its pause_id names sorts right after that pause (several such resumes by lowercase id). Roles outside [start, terminal.at] are skipped; they get no effect. A gap pause opens a pause if none is open and takes it over (pause id = the stop's); a gap resume ends whatever pause is open. User events: void `before_start` if at < start; `after_stop` if at > terminal.at; `too_long` if at > start + max_run_ms; a removed event is `deleted` (a removed lap whose seg matched becomes a ghost (lap.at, remove.at)); a resume naming a removed pause is `deleted`; next/lap/skip with seg != expected: `stale`, where expected = closed segments + ghosts with ghost.at < at < ghost.removed_at. next closes the open segment and opens the next pending step (a lap when none is left); lap closes it and opens a lap (pending unchanged). skip on a step segment must name that step (else `stale`): it joins `skipped` and the open segment is relabelled to the next pending step (or a lap); skip on a lap: `no_step` if nothing is pending, `stale` unless it names the head of pending, which joins `skipped`. pause: `already_paused` if paused. resume: `not_paused` if not paused, `stale` unless pause_id is the open pause's id; else the pause [paused_since, at) closes.

Terminal stop: an open pause ends at the stop, the open segment closes at it, status `stopped` (the server says `finishing` while required answers are missing). Discard: status `discarded`, no open segment or pause. Otherwise `paused` or `running`.

Segments: pauses stay whole; a segment's paused_ms is its overlap with them (an open pause covers up to the segment's end: measure it to that end, not to a large sentinel), active_ms = length - paused_ms. Lap n (n counting lap segments from 1 in segment order, the open one included) has lap_type = laps[(n-1) mod |laps|].key and label '{that label} {(n-1) div |laps| + 1}', or lap_type null and 'Lap n' with no lap types; steps have lap_type null. open.index = closed segment count; next_step = head of pending while the run is open, else null. A segment's event_id/opened_by name the event that opened it (null/'start' for the first); a pause's id is its pause event's (a gap pause's is its stop's). terminal_id = the terminal stop's id (null unless stopped); lap_count = closed lap segments; next_lap_type = the type of lap number lap_count + (open is a lap ? 1 : 0) + 1 while open and typed, else null.
Instants out: UTC, 'Z', six fraction digits only when the millisecond part is not zero (how the API writes them). Compare by parsing to milliseconds or as strings.

timing (stopped runs only): started_at, ended_at, paused_ms = sum of pauses, active_ms = ended - started - paused_ms, complete = the version has no steps, or every one of its steps has a segment and none was skipped; edited = false; and the state's segments, skipped, pauses and terminal_id.
timings: stored entry timings as clients decode them; `expected` is the timing as served. A pre-v2 timing's terminal_id, lap_type, event_id, opened_by and pause ids read null.
